title: 2D Sources & Visual Generators
intro: Every visual patch starts somewhere. These nodes make the first picture, from a photo on disk to a shape drawn from pure math, that everything downstream gets to distort, color, and remix.
cards: Drag a photo, PNG, JPEG, TIFF, or BMP straight from Finder onto the canvas and it becomes a live texture. This is the simplest way to get your own artwork, logo, or photography into a patch.
drop in a piece of your own art and run it through a Kaleidoscope for an instant looping visual.
Plays back any movie file as a live texture, with a Loop switch and a speed dial, crank speed negative and it plays backwards. The simplest way to get found footage moving inside a patch.
set Speed to a small negative value for a slow, unsettling reverse loop.

Captures a live feed straight from your Mac's camera, the built-in FaceTime HD camera, an external USB webcam, or a Continuity Camera iPhone, with a device picker, a resolution choice, and a mirror toggle for when a front-facing camera reads reversed.
mirror the feed and route it through Feedback for an instant infinity-mirror selfie loop.

Pulls a live video feed straight out of another app publishing over the macOS Syphon protocol, OBS, Resolume, TouchDesigner, with no re-encoding. Great for bringing a camera feed or another VJ tool into Infinite's node graph.
pipe your webcam through OBS, then Syphon it in and cut yourself out with Remove Background.

Draws crisp, perfectly smooth vector shapes out of pure math, 20 primitives from simple circles and stars to hearts, gears, and blobs, no pixelation no matter how big you scale them. Fill, stroke, and roundness are all wide open.
wire an LFO into Size so a circle breathes in and out on its own, then glow it up with Bloom.

Generates organic, ever-shifting texture, soft clouds, ridged terrain, cell-like Voronoi and Worley patterns, or plain white static, from six procedural noise algorithms. It's the visual equivalent of static: raw material for almost everything else.
feed Noise into a 3D Plane's height so the terrain rolls and drifts like real landscape.

A pattern factory with ten procedural surfaces on tap, bricks, cell clusters, swirling marble, wood grain, wave bands, checkers, clouds, and rocky Musgrave terrain, all generated live rather than loaded from a file, so they can be animated forever.
run a Brick pattern through Color Ramp to turn plain masonry into a stylized sunset gradient.
A clean two-color gradient, linear, radial, angular, diamond, or spiral. Perfect as a soft backdrop, a mask, or a blend driver for another effect.
multiply a radial Ramp over live video to vignette the edges of frame automatically.

A shader playground with more than two dozen ready-made looks baked in, plasma fields, Mandelbrot and Julia fractals, Truchet tiles, Voronoi cells, phyllotaxis spirals, each with four knobs you can wire up to anything else in the patch. For when you want something nobody else's patch has.
route your track's energy level into one of Formula's knobs so the pattern pulses with the mix.

A live paint canvas right inside the node graph, soft round, hard round, square, spray, chalk, and ink-bleed brushes, plus a dedicated eraser toggle. Anything you paint becomes a texture the rest of the patch can use immediately.
paint a quick stroke and route it through Feedback so every mark trails and echoes forever.

title: Typography & Text
intro: Words, on screen or in space. Both nodes read every font already installed on your Mac.
cards: Renders crisp type using any font installed on your Mac via CoreText, titles, lyrics, captions. Alignment, size, and letter spacing are all adjustable live.
drop a title at the top of your Layer Stack and hit it with Bloom for a glowing lower-third.
Takes the same lettering and extrudes it into a real, beveled 3D mesh you can light, rotate, and shade like any other object in the scene, logo stings and title cards with actual depth.
give your extruded word a Gold Chrome material and spin it slowly under a studio HDRI.

title: 2D Image Effects, Blur, Warp & Glow
intro: Take any picture, a photo, a video, a shape, a render, and push it somewhere else. These sit in the middle of a chain, one image cable in and one out, so you can stack as many as you like. The next chapter lists every remaining filter on the shelf.
cards: Two separate blur nodes for smoothing an image out, soft focus, depth-of-field, or just taking the edge off something too sharp. Often used right before a Bloom to make the glow itself feel softer.
blur at a low radius before Bloom for a dreamy, filmic haze instead of a harsh glow.
Streaks an image in one direction, mimicking a fast camera pan or a subject moving quicker than the shutter can freeze. Instant sense of speed.
screen-blend a motion-blurred copy of your video back over the original for a racing-game feel.
Blurs outward from a single focal point you can place anywhere on screen, the classic zoom-punch effect used to slam attention onto one spot.
trigger a quick burst of Radial Blur on every kick drum hit for a punch-in feel.

Two related nodes that make bright areas glow and bleed light into their surroundings, the way a real camera lens does when it looks at something dazzling. One of the fastest ways to make flat visuals feel expensive.
drop Bloom right before your Output on almost any visual patch, it rarely looks worse.

Six flavors of broken-signal chaos, sliced frames, RGB channel splitting, scanlines, blocky corruption, waving distortion, and full datamosh. Dial it from a subtle VHS wobble to full digital meltdown.
fire Glitch's Amount from every drum hit so the visuals corrupt exactly on the beat.

Three separate optical-warp nodes: Twirl spins a vortex around a center point, Pinch/Punch magnifies or implodes like a lens, and Ripple sends concentric water rings out from a point. Chain any of them together for compound warps.
map your Macro XY trackpad to Twirl's angle and "paint" the swirl live during a performance.
Slices the frame into mirrored wedges around a center point, instantly turning ordinary footage into a mandala.
point a webcam or Syphon feed straight into Kaleidoscope for an endless, hypnotic VJ loop.

title: 2D Image Effects, The Full Filter Shelf
intro: Infinite's image filters all share one C++ node class, but each of the 34 entries below spawns as its own node in the palette. The seven in Chapter Three got the full treatment; here's the rest of the shelf, one line each, straight from the shader source.
All 34 entries live in one shared table in the app's source; here they are grouped roughly by what they do, distortion & detail, color, and compositing & glow.
rows: Unsharp Mask
Sharpens the image by comparing it to a blurred version of itself and boosting the difference, controlled by Amount and Radius.
Pixelate
Blocks the image into large flat squares to create a chunky, mosaic look, sized by Block Size.
Add Noise
Sprinkles random per-pixel grain onto the image, with Amount controlling how strong the speckling is.
Vignette
Darkens the corners and edges around a center point, with Amount for strength and Radius/Softness for how far the darkening spreads.
Transform
Moves, scales, and rotates the whole image using Translate, Scale, and Rotation controls, leaving anything pushed outside the frame transparent.
Lens Distortion
Bulges or pinches the image like a camera lens and fringes the edges with color, controlled by Barrel curvature and Chromatic Aberration amount.
Displace
Pushes pixels sideways using either a second connected image as a displacement map or, with nothing plugged in, an animated wavy pattern.
Liquify
Warps the image with a smooth, flowing animated distortion like moving liquid, shaped by Amount, Scale, and Speed.
Symmetry
Mirrors one half of the image onto the other across a chosen axis and center point, with an option to flip the whole result.
Crop
Trims the edges of the image by set Left/Right/Top/Bottom amounts, then either leaves the trimmed area transparent, zooms in to fill the frame, or fills it with a solid color.
Emboss
Turns the image into a raised, carved-relief look by comparing pixels on either side of a light direction, with Amount and Angle controlling depth and lighting.
Convolve
Runs a custom 3×3 grid of numbers over every pixel and its neighbors, letting you dial in blur, sharpen, edge, or emboss-style looks from nine kernel values.
Halftone
Recreates the image using a grid of dots sized by brightness (like a newspaper print), with Scale controlling dot density.
LUT
Applies a color lookup table by wiring in a second texture as the LUT reference, the same idea colorists use for film-stock emulation.
Lookup
A related color-remap node that reads a reference gradient/table image to redirect each pixel's color.
Gradient Map
Recolors the image by mapping its brightness onto a custom two-color (or multi-stop) gradient.
Posterize
Reduces the image to a limited number of tonal steps per channel for a flat, poster-print look.
Threshold
Converts the image to pure black and white based on a brightness cutoff point.
Exposure
Brightens or darkens the whole image in stops, the same control a camera's exposure dial gives you.
Invert
Flips every color to its opposite, turning the image into its photographic negative.
Outer Glow
Adds a soft colored glow that blooms outward from the image's edges or transparency, with Amount for strength and Color for tint.
Color Overlay
Tints the whole image toward a single flat color, with Opacity controlling how strongly the tint replaces the original colors.
Drop Shadow
Casts a soft offset shadow of the image's silhouette behind it, with Offset X/Y for direction and distance and Opacity/Color for its look.

title: Color Grading & Tone Mapping
intro: The finishing pass. Once the image is built, these nodes shape its mood, from a quick contrast bump to a full cinema-grade film look.
cards: Your all-in-one grading desk: brightness, contrast, levels, color balance, hue, saturation, vibrance, and a black-and-white switch, the same toolkit colorists use, chained together in one node.
warm the shadows and cool the highlights for an instant "teal and orange" cinematic grade.
Draggable tone curves for the combined RGB channel plus red, green, and blue individually, the precise, hands-on way to push contrast or introduce a color cast exactly where you want it.
pull an S-curve on the RGB channel to punch up contrast on flat, washed-out noise textures.
Recolors any grayscale source by mapping its brightness onto a custom gradient with up to 32 stops, the classic trick for turning plain noise or a height map into something that looks painted.
map noise through a five-stop sunset gradient, then use the result as a material's color.

Applies a color lookup table to your image by wiring in a second texture as the LUT reference, the same underlying idea colorists use for film-stock emulation, driven from an image input rather than a loaded file.
wire a strip-LUT texture into your final Render 3D pass for a consistent, repeatable grade.

title: Compositing & Layering
intro: Where multiple pictures become one, and where you keep a busy graph readable. Everything here speaks the peach Image cable.
cards: Combines two images with a wide range of blend modes, Multiply, Screen, Overlay, and more, plus an opacity dial. This is how you layer a glowing shape over live video, or double-expose two textures.
screen-blend a glowing shape over live video for a lightweight double-exposure look.

A multi-layer compositor with per-layer blend mode, opacity, and visibility, think of it as a mini layers panel living inside your node graph, for building a full scene from separate pieces without a tangle of individual Blend nodes.
stack a 3D background, particles, live video, and a text title into one finished frame.

Resizes and reflows whatever image comes in to a target width and height, with a mode of Fit (letterbox), Fill (crop to fill), Stretch (ignore aspect ratio), or Native (pass through). A background color and opacity fill any letterboxed edges.
feed a portrait-shaped camera or image source into a square canvas using Fill mode so it crops to a clean center square.

Cycles automatically among up to 4 connected image inputs on a timed interval (beats or seconds, synced to the transport), with a crossfade control blending the outgoing and incoming input, or a manual toggle to freeze on one chosen slot.
wire four different visual "looks" in and set it to switch every 8 beats with a short crossfade for an automatically evolving VJ set.
A zero-cost reroute point: it simply reports whatever texture is plugged into it as its own output, without rendering anything itself. Meant purely for tidying up cable runs in a busy patch.
insert one at a junction where several cables cross so the wiring reads cleanly instead of crisscrossing.

Functionally identical to Null (a free pass-through, no processing) but drawn with a large canvas, so you can actually inspect the image at a given stage of a patch instead of judging it from a tiny thumbnail.
drop one mid-chain in a long effects stack to see exactly what the image looks like before the next step touches it.

A resizable, colored backdrop for organizing the node editor, not a functional processing node, it has no output of its own. Any node sitting inside it gets dragged along when you move the group's header.
wrap a whole "generator" section of a big patch in a Group so you can drag the entire subsystem around at once.
A plain annotation box, it does no image processing at all and produces no output. It just holds a block of text plus its own size and background color so you can label or explain parts of a patch.
drop one next to a complex chain to leave yourself a note about what a tricky setting does.

title: Feedback, Trails & AI Vision
intro: Nodes that feed an image back into itself, or reach for on-device machine vision, turning one frame into an ever- evolving loop.
cards: Uses Apple's on-device Vision framework to cut a subject or person cleanly out of a live camera feed, no green screen required. Runs fast enough for live performance, with adjustable feather, threshold, and contrast on the cut edge.
drop yourself into a rotating 3D starfield with nothing but a webcam.

Two related nodes that feed a frame back into itself with a slight zoom, spin, or fade, the same trick behind classic video-feedback tunnels. Every new stroke or shape leaves a trail that spirals off into infinity.
paint one stroke on the Draw canvas and watch Feedback turn it into an endless spiral.
Simulates the same Gray-Scott chemistry that grows animal spots, coral, and cellular patterns in nature, feed it a nudge and organic, living patterns spread and evolve on their own.
color-map the result and use it as a slowly-crawling texture on a 3D material.

An iterative image mutator: instead of reprocessing the original source each frame, it feeds its own previous output back into itself and mutates it again, so the image drifts progressively further from the source over generations. An XY pad cross-fades between eight mutation operators, and its motion can be recorded and looped.
record a slow FX-pad path with high feedback and low source-pull, then loop it so the image evolves through the same mutation journey every cycle.

title: 3D Building Blocks & Materials
intro: Meshes and the surfaces they wear. These nodes speak the green Geometry cable, and everything eventually plugs into Render 3D to become a picture.
cards: A deep library of 3D building blocks, cube, sphere, icosphere, cylinder, cone, torus, plane, disc, and more exotic forms like torus knots and Möbius strips, with adjustable tessellation so they stay smooth up close.
drop a sphere, give it a Chrome material, and light it under an HDRI for an instant hero shot.

Imports your own 3D models, OBJ, PLY, STL, or USD/USDZ, with automatic centering and scale normalization, so anything exported from Blender or elsewhere just drops in and works. (glTF and FBX aren't supported yet.)
import a character model and spin it live using a rotation modulated by an LFO.

Overrides the surface material of whatever geometry passes through it, so one authored look can be shared by several shapes. Exposes a full PBR set, color, metallic, roughness, opacity, emission, IOR, transmission, clearcoat, sheen, iridescence, and can take up to eight image inputs to paint any of those channels from a texture.
feed a Noise texture into the roughness map input to give a single flat color a hand-worn, uneven sheen.

Physically pushes a mesh's vertices using a texture, real 3D geometry displacement, distinct from the 2D Displace/Liquify image filters, which only warp a flat image and never move actual geometry. Offsets vertices by a strength and midlevel, with flat-shading and normal-flip options.
drive it with a slow-animated Noise texture to make a flat plane ripple like disturbed water.

Changes how a material's texture maps are looked up on a surface without altering the mesh itself, UV, Generated, or Object coordinate space, plus per-axis offset, rotation, scale, and a triplanar-blend control.
switch to Object space and animate the rotate values to make a tiled pattern slowly spin across a surface independent of its own transform.

Conforms one mesh onto the surface of another, every source vertex moves to the nearest point on the target's surface, real shrinkwrap-style deformation. Offers Cylindrical, Spherical, and Nearest Surface modes plus a bend radius and blend amount.
wrap a flat text mesh cylindrically around a bottle-shaped target so the text reads as if printed on the label.

Generates a spline that works two ways: as visible tube geometry (adjustable radius, sides, taper) and as a path other nodes can follow. Builds from up to 8 control points using Catmull-Rom, Bezier, B-spline, or linear interpolation, closeable into a loop.
set it to a closed loop and route a Path-follower along it to fly a camera or object in a continuous circuit.

A pure pass-through for a geometry cable, forwards the mesh, material, and mapping from its single input unchanged. Exists purely to route or organize a 3D chain, the geometry equivalent of the plain Null node.
use it as a labeled junction point where a rig's main geometry chain splits off to several downstream effects.

title: 3D Points, Instancing & Mesh Ops
intro: Scatter, stamp, and clean up geometry at scale, the toolkit for turning one shape into a thousand, or a cloud of points into solid form.
cards: Stamps a copy of one mesh onto the points of another, turning a single object into a scattered crowd drawn as GPU instances, one draw call for thousands of copies. Points can come from vertices, edges, faces, or a point cloud, with per-instance scale/rotation randomization and normal alignment.
scatter thousands of tiny cubes across a sphere's surface with align-to-normal on so they bristle outward like fur.

Scatters points evenly across the surface area of an input mesh (area-weighted, not vertex-based) so coverage stays uniform even on meshes with uneven face sizes. Offers Random or Poisson Disk (even minimum spacing) methods.
scatter Poisson-Disk points across a terrain mesh's faces for evenly spaced grass instances with no clumping.

Generates a plain rectangular lattice of points from scratch, no geometry input needed, with adjustable count, spacing, jitter, and per-point size. Its point ordering deliberately matches Image to Points, so the two line up point-for- point at equal counts.
build a 20×20 point grid and instance small spheres on it for a uniform matrix-style array.

Converts an image into a point cloud, one particle per sampled pixel on a density grid, with brightness pushing each point out of a flat plane by a depth amount, and darker pixels dropped entirely so a cutout image reads as a shape.
feed a photo of a face in and instance small spheres on the points to build a pointillist 3D portrait.
Converts an incoming point cloud into a bare mesh made only of vertices, no edges, no faces, so cloud data can re- enter mesh-only operators like Merge by Distance.
turn a Particle System's live cloud into vertices, then run it through Merge by Distance to weld nearby particles into clusters.
Writes a color onto every vertex or particle of whatever geometry feeds it, from a flat color, a position/normal-driven gradient ramp, per-element random color, a palette swatch, or a texture lookup.
feed a Distribute Points node in with source set to Position for a smooth color gradient across a scattered field.
Merges up to four geometry inputs into a single mesh, using plain concatenation or real CSG Union/Intersect/Difference. Each input's own transform is baked in before combining.
feed two overlapping spheres in Difference mode to carve a hole through one with the other.

Welds vertices that lie within a threshold distance of each other, the cleanup pass that closes seams left behind by a scatter or conversion node, or, cranked up, collapses geometry together outright.
run Points to Vertices output through Merge by Distance with a larger threshold to fuse nearby particles into solid clumps.

Generates blobs that smoothly merge into one another rather than intersecting with hard edges, surfaced via marching cubes over a summed field of up to 8 balls. Can also take a point-cloud input, letting a particle system be surfaced as a liquid-like blob.
feed a particle emitter's point cloud in to turn a scattering of points into a single flowing liquid mass.

The 3D counterpart to the image Resynth node, each generation mutates the previous generation, not the original input, so the mesh drifts progressively over time via displace, jitter, smooth, twist, bulge, extrude, subdivide, and squash operators.
set a high displace weight and low smooth weight, then auto-step it to slowly grow an organic, coral-like form from a simple starting mesh.

title: 3D Simulation, Scene & Render
intro: Physics, the camera, the lights, and the render pass that turns geometry into a picture.
cards: A physically-inspired ocean built from real Gerstner wave mathematics, tune amplitude, wavelength, steepness, direction, choppiness, and speed for anything from glassy calm to a churning storm.
drive wave amplitude straight from your track's bass so the sea swells with the low end.

Takes any mesh, usually a flat plane, and drapes it like real fabric using position-based dynamics, with stiffness, damping, mass, gravity, and wind you can push around live for anything from a stiff flag to a silky drape.
crank wind sideways and watch a plane billow like a flag caught in a gust.
Spawns and simulates a stream of moving points with adjustable emit rate, lifetime, initial speed, and turbulence, sparks, dust, snow, or drifting motes, all reacting in real time.
trigger a burst of particles on every kick drum for a fireworks-on-the-beat effect.

Defines the viewpoint for Render 3D, perspective or orthographic, field of view, distance/azimuth/elevation orbit around a target, roll, and clip planes. An orbit-per-beat value spins the camera automatically for turntable shots.
set orbit-per-beat to a nonzero value for an automatic slow turntable rotation, synced to the transport clock.

Defines a single light source for Render 3D, Directional, Point, Sun, Ambient, or Spot, with azimuth/elevation/distance placement, color, intensity, falloff, and cone angle/softness for spots. Can also orbit automatically over time.
use a Spot light with a narrow cone angle and low penumbra for a hard-edged theatrical spotlight look.

Loads an equirectangular HDR/EXR image and hands it to Render 3D as a real image-based environment, replacing the built-in sky gradient. Exposes intensity and a rotation so you can dial in brightness and spin where reflections and light come from.
load an HDRI of a sunset and slowly animate its rotation to sweep studio-quality reflections across a metallic object.

Cycles between up to four connected 3D geometry inputs, forwarding whichever is currently active rather than blending them, a hard cut, timed by beats/seconds or set manually. The geometry-side counterpart to the image Switcher.
wire four different Geometry shapes into the four slots and let it hard-cut between them every 2 beats for a stop- motion-style shape change.

Deforms a mesh in real time from live audio, with five modes: waveform push, FFT-spectrum warp, concentric ripples, Chladni-plate standing-wave patterns, or a straight axis push. Includes attack/decay smoothing and a real-time subdivision level.
patch a kick-drum track in using Acoustic Ripples mode to make a sphere pulse outward on every hit.

Builds its own ribbon-shaped mesh directly from an audio signal, no upstream geometry needed. Width, height scale, segment count, gain, and smoothing are all adjustable, alongside its own transform and material.
route a vocal track in and place several ribbons at different rotations to build a waveform sculpture.

The camera and lighting engine that turns every 3D node into a real picture, physically-based Cook-Torrance/GGX materials, ACES tonemapping, and MSAA antialiasing, all live, with up to 4 geometry inputs plus camera, light, and HDRI. This is where the green Geometry cables turn back into a peach Image cable.
plug in geometry, a material, a light, and an HDRI, then send the result straight into Bloom.

title: Audio Synthesizers
intro: Where sound is born. These nodes turn silence, or notes coming in from an arpeggiator or MIDI controller, into audio you can hear and process.
cards: The flagship synthesizer: 64 wavetables you can morph smoothly between across 8 frames, up to 8-voice unison for thickness, a resonant filter, and three independent ADSR envelopes shaping amplitude, filter, and pitch over time.
modulate the table-morph position with an LFO for a synth patch that never quite settles.

A single-voice synth on the wavetable engine, offering four waveforms (Sine, Triangle, Saw, Square) with pitch, glide, pitch bend, and an audio-rate FM/PM input whose depth and mode you control directly.
patch a second Oscillator into the FM input and sweep FM depth for classic bell/metallic tones.

Turns any 2D image or video texture into a "terrain" surface and reads audio by tracing a closed orbit across it, Circle, Lissajous, Lemniscate, Spiral, or Scanline, with full unison, an amp envelope, and a multi-mode filter.
feed a slowly-animating Reaction Diffusion texture in and let scan speed drift the orbit for an evolving drone.

A Desmos-style oscillator: type a formula like y = sin(x + a) and it renders that curve as an anti-aliased, polyphonic wavetable waveform, so turning knobs A through D actually reshapes the wave's math instead of just modulating a fixed one. A full voice sits behind it, unison, an amp envelope, and a resonant filter with its own envelope.
start from a plain sine and add a small a * sin(x * 3) term for an instantly richer, custom waveform.

Reads an image as a spectrogram: it scans horizontally while each row of pixels defines the amplitude of one of a bank of up to 256 sine partials, so a picture's brightness pattern literally becomes the sound's harmonic content.
draw a simple shape in a Draw node and route it in, the silhouette becomes an audible spectral sweep as the playhead crosses it.

Physically models how real metal and glass actually ring when struck, eight material presets from Steel and Bell Bronze to Glass/Crystal and Vibraphone Bar, a genuinely resonant, inharmonic decay rather than a synthetic approximation.
trigger it from Bouncing Balls for a gamelan-like patter of chiming, decaying notes.

Load a file or record incoming audio, then play it back one-shot or looping (forward, reversed, or ping-pong) with independent pitch, finetune, and varispeed, and two playback lanes, polyphonic (MIDI-driven) and monophonic (free- running).
record a vocal phrase via record-in, then trigger it polyphonically from MIDI Notes with pitch mapped per key.

Chops a loaded or recorded sample into slices, either by onset detection or by a grid locked to the transport tempo, and maps them chromatically across the keyboard starting at middle C, the classic MPC/Simpler-style chop workflow.
record a spoken phrase, slice it by onset, and play the syllables back in a new order from MIDI Notes.

A real-time granular synthesizer that shreds a loaded or recorded sample into micro-grains and re-stitches them, with grain length, density, scan speed/position (with freeze), and stochastic randomization on position, length, pitch, and pan.
load a field recording, freeze the scan, and crank the position/pitch randomization for a shimmering granular cloud from a single still moment.

Stretches any audio file up to 1000 times longer without changing its pitch, turning a two-second vocal snippet into an hours-long, slowly shifting ambient texture. The classic "everything sounds like a choir of angels" trick.
stretch a spoken-word sample 20x and drown it in reverb for an instant soundscape bed.

An evolving sound-design tool: it decomposes a recorded sample into tracked harmonic partials plus residual noise, then Roll mutates a parameter genome and re-renders a new sample from that, each roll drifting further from the last, not from the original source.
record a found sound, then hit Roll a dozen times in a row and listen to it wander into something alien.

Slices audio into overlapping grains, measures each one's loudness, brightness, or a random tag, and re-orders them along a blend between the original chronological order and a fully metric-sorted arrangement, at full amount it turns any recording into a rising or falling contour.
sort by Level and crank Amount to turn a busy loop into a smooth, swelling riser.
An 8-track, 8-step sequencer for your own samples, complete with swing groove, mutes, and solos, build a full beat without leaving the canvas, and tap any lane's trigger to drive visuals too.
send the kick lane's trigger into a Glitch node so the picture stutters with the beat.

title: Audio Effects & Plugin Hosting
intro: Shape sound after it's been made, filters, space, grit, and a doorway to Audio Units already installed on your Mac. Like the image filter shelf, every effect below shares one C++ class but spawns as its own node.
cards: A classic analog-style filter with 12 types on tap, low-pass and high-pass at 12/24/36 dB per octave, band-pass, notch, shelves, and peak, with an envelope follower for auto-wah and a sidechain input so another sound can sweep the cutoff for you.
sweep the cutoff with an LFO for a slow, breathing filter-sweep synth part.
A five-band studio equalizer with a live filter-response curve you can see and drag, carve out mud, add air, or fix a harsh frequency, watching the curve move as you turn each knob.
scoop the low-mids on your master bus before it hits a Limiter for extra clarity.
Loads any Audio Unit you already own, synth or effect, right into the graph, with its native interface and up to 32 of its parameters exposed for modulation like any other Infinite node.
load your favorite Audio Unit synth and drive it straight from the Arpeggiator.
A tempo-synced ping-pong delay with feedback, tone shaping, panning, and ducking, everything from a tight slapback to a rhythmic, bouncing echo.
set the rate division to a dotted-eighth for a classic, rhythmic bouncing echo.
An algorithmic reverb with room size, decay time, damping, pre-delay, and stereo width, a wash big enough to sound like a cathedral, or small enough to feel like a tiled room.
stack Reverb after Delay for echoes that themselves bloom into space.
Warm analog-style tube-and-transistor saturation with drive, bias, tone, and color controls, a gentle glow at low settings, real grit when you push it.
hit a drum mix with a few dB of Drive for extra punch and glue.
A separate lo-fi crusher: independent sample-rate (down to 200 Hz) and bit-depth (down to 1 bit) reduction for anything from a subtle vintage-sampler grit to full digital destruction.
crush a clean synth line down to 8 bits for an instant retro-game feel.

Runs a Field kernel once per audio sample as a custom effect you write yourself, declare a bit of state for a delay line or filter memory, declare a param for an automatic modulatable knob, and write the DSP math directly instead of hunting for the right built-in. See Chapter Twenty for the Field language itself.
write a simple one-pole low-pass in a few lines and compare it against the built-in Audio Filter.
rows: Dynamics
A compressor that squashes loud peaks down once they cross a Threshold, tightening dynamics by a set Ratio, with Attack/Release/Makeup rounding out the feel.
Limiter
A brick-wall ceiling that catches anything above the Threshold and prevents it from getting louder, with In/Out Gain to drive it harder or make up level.
Stereo
Widens or narrows the stereo image with a Width knob (0 collapses to mono), plus Pan and a Bass Mono control that keeps low end centered.
Pitch Shifter
Shifts pitch up or down by semitones (up to two octaves either way) using a delay-line pitch shifter, with Grain size shaping the artifacts.
Chorus
Thickens the sound with multiple slightly detuned, delayed copies, with Delay time and Depth of the wobble and a free or tempo-synced Rate.
Flanger
Creates a sweeping, jet-plane whoosh by mixing a short modulating delay with Feedback back into the signal.
Phaser
Sweeps notches through the sound for a swirling effect, set by a Cutoff center frequency, Depth, and Rate.
Transient Shaper
Reshapes the punch of a sound by independently boosting or cutting the Attack (the initial hit) and the Sustain (the tail).
Stutter
Repeats a short slice of audio like a glitchy loop, with tempo-synced or free timing and a step/gate mask controlling which repeats play.
Ring Mod
Multiplies the signal by an oscillator to produce bell-like, metallic, robotic tones, with adjustable frequency and waveform.
Frequency Shifter
Shifts every frequency in the sound up or down by a fixed Hz amount (not musically, like pitch), creating inharmonic textures, with Feedback adding spiraling "barber pole" motion.
Tremolo
Pulses the volume up and down with an LFO, set by Depth and a free or tempo-synced Rate.
Formant Filter
Gives the sound a vowel-like, talking/singing quality by morphing between A-E-I-O-U formant shapes, with Q controlling resonance.
Wavetable Shaper
Distorts the sound by running it through a chosen wavetable, with Table picking the waveform set, Position scanning through it, and Drive controlling intensity.
notes: The Audio Effects category holds 20 entries sharing one DSP-hosting node class; the seven above got the full treatment, here's the rest of the shelf.

title: Audio Utility & Routing
intro: The plumbing that gets sound in, mixed, split, and out, plus two nodes for turning sound into a picture.
cards: A simple audio level control: one dB knob raises or lowers the volume of the signal running through it, with an inline meter showing the output level.
turn a hot oscillator or sampler down a few dB before it hits a Mixer so it doesn't clip.
Taps the computer's live input device (microphone or line-in) and brings it into the patch, with a gain trim and its own input-level meter.
feed a live microphone into a reactive visual patch so the visuals respond to whatever's happening in the room.
The terminal endpoint of an audio chain, takes exactly one audio input and sends it to the real output device, and can record straight to a file in WAV, FLAC, or MP3.
route your final mixed signal here and hit record in FLAC to capture a lossless bounce of a live performance.
The app's dedicated summing node, taking up to 8 input slots, each with its own gain, pan, and mute, plus a per-channel peak meter and an overall summed-output meter.
pan several looped instrument stems across the stereo field and mute/unmute them live to build up an arrangement.
The explicit fan-out point for audio: since an audio output can only feed one destination, Splitter takes one input and makes it available to up to 4 downstream consumers as a passthrough copy.
split one synth's output to feed both a Mixer channel and a separate effects-only chain in parallel.
A two-input crossfader with a single Blend control: 0 plays only input A, 1 plays only input B, and 0.5 gives an equal- power blend of both.
crossfade smoothly between two different loops by automating the Blend knob over a bar.
Turns an incoming audio signal into an image, rendering either a live Waveform or a Spectrum (FFT) view into a GPU texture, with adjustable FFT window size and smoothing.
feed a bassline in using Spectrum mode with high smoothing for a slowly pulsing frequency-bar texture to layer under other visuals.

Splits incoming audio into up to 8 frequency bands and maps each one to a color, Intensity mode glows a stop brighter with its band's energy, Expansion widens it, and Spectrum paints a continuous FFT sweep across the palette. Patch an image in and it grades that image through the audio-reactive gradient instead of outputting the gradient alone.
leave the image input empty and use it as a standalone audio-reactive gradient background.

title: MIDI & Note Shaping
intro: The note stream comes in from a keyboard or controller; these nodes reshape it, filtering, transposing, humanizing, and timing-correcting, before it reaches a synth. All flow over the lavender Note cable.
cards: The note source, reads live MIDI input and turns it into note events for the rest of the chain, with a channel selector, a transpose knob, a velocity scale, and an option to snap incoming notes to the global key/scale. An input device dropdown picks which controller it listens to (or all of them), and Learn sets the device and channel from the next key you play.
press Learn and play a key on each of two controllers, one Midi Notes per controller, to layer them into different chains without them colliding.
A gate on which notes get through, combining a scale/key filter, a pitch range, and a percent chance, a note only passes if it clears all three checks.
set a low chance percentage to turn a busy MIDI part into a sparse, randomly-thinned one.

Shifts every note by a fixed number of semitones, with an option to snap the result to the global scale. The shift is applied once at note-on and remembered for that note, so a held note's release always lands on the matching pitch.
stack two Note Transpose nodes at +12 and -12 semitones off the same MIDI source to build instant octave doubling.
A live pitch-bend knob (±2 semitones) that adds into each note's continuous bend amount rather than re-triggering the note, so moving it while a note is held slides that note's pitch in real time.
automate the bend knob for a slow pitch-drift or vibrato-like wobble on a sustained note.
Reshapes how hard you hit the keys maps to output velocity, using a single curve exponent, below 1 boosts soft hits, above 1 favors hard hits.
set the curve well below 1 to make a light, breathy playing style trigger notes at near-full velocity.
Controls how long each note rings out with a single hold-time knob. At 0 it's a passthrough; above 0 it ignores the real note-off and schedules its own fixed duration for every note.
set a short fixed hold time to turn held chords into a clean, staccato pattern.
Adds random imperfection to a note stream with two independent knobs: timing jitter (when a note actually fires) and velocity jitter (how hard it hits). Both default to off.
add a little timing and velocity jitter to a rigid quantized sequence to make it feel played by hand.
Snaps each note-on forward in time to the nearest grid line, never earlier than when the note actually arrived, at a chosen musical division.
use a coarse quantize division to lock loose, off-grid playing onto the beat without losing the original note order.
Fills the gap between one played note and the next with a fast run of very short in-between notes, approximating a portamento slide since the note system has no continuous pitch to bend smoothly.
set the glide time to around 300–500ms on a bass line for a slippery, portamento-like slide between notes.
Repeats every incoming note a set number of times, each repeat spaced further apart, getting quieter and optionally shifting in pitch. The original note always plays first unchanged.
use a short delay with a +12 semitone shift per repeat to turn single notes into an ascending octave echo trail.

title: Generative & Physical Note Nodes
intro: Nodes that write their own music, from a classic arpeggio pattern to a physics playground that composes melodies from bouncing balls, plus the mergers and switchers that manage several note streams at once.
cards: Takes held notes and breaks them into a rhythmic, tempo-locked pattern, Up, Down, Up-Down, Random, As-Played, and a dozen more traversal modes, with 1 to 4 octaves of range.
hold a chord from Chorder and let the Arpeggiator turn it into a driving pattern.
Turns a single held note into a full chord, with adjustable chord size, a strum offset, humanized timing and velocity, and scale quantization so nothing plays a wrong note.
play a single key and let Chorder voice it into a lush, gently strummed chord for an instant pad.
A dedicated step sequencer for melody, up to 16 steps, each with its own note, velocity, and on/off toggle, plus a gate- length control for how long each step rings out.
program a simple 8-step bassline and send it straight into a synth for an instant groove.

A physics playground that turns bouncing balls into music, balls glide inside a container shape and fire a note, quantized to a musical scale, every time they hit a wall. Gravity doesn't pull them down; the bounce pattern writes the melody.
set the scale to Minor Pentatonic and let the balls compose a hypnotic, generative loop.

The system's note fan-out node: one input split across four separate outputs, chosen by Round Robin, Random, Probability, or Chain mode. A note's matching note-off always replays to the same output it was sent to.
use Round Robin mode to alternate incoming notes between four different synths for a call-and-response texture.

The note system's fan-in counterpart to Note Router: merges up to 4 note streams into one output in timestamp order, keeping each input's notes as independent voices so two sources playing the same pitch at once sound as two overlapping notes instead of colliding.
merge a live keyboard and an Arpeggiator into one stream so you can play live over your own pattern.

The note-cable counterpart of the image and 3D Switcher, cycles between up to four connected note sources on a timed interval or a manual slot, so a synth downstream hears only whichever source is currently active.
wire four different sequencers in and let it hard-cut between them every 4 beats for an evolving arrangement.

A self-running generator that produces its own note stream via a bounded random walk, each new note is the previous note plus a small random offset, clamped and quantized to a chosen scale and root. No note input needed.
set a narrow pitch range with a small max step for a meandering, ambient melodic line that never strays far.
Layers up to 8 extra transposed copies on top of every note that passes through, with the original note always passing through underneath. Each voice has its own semitone offset and on/off switch.
enable the +12 and +7 voice offsets to turn single played notes into instant octave-and-fifth power chords.

Records whatever note stream feeds it, with tempo-relative timing so it stays in sync even if the BPM changes, then loops that recording back on top of the live input, which always keeps passing through.
record a short improvised phrase, then keep playing live on top while it loops underneath.
Takes a chord's simultaneous notes and spreads their onsets across time in ascending pitch order, like a strummed guitar, while keeping each note's original gate length intact.
feed it block chords and set the spacing to 20–40ms for a natural strummed-guitar feel instead of a stabbed chord.

title: Modulators, Shape & Combine
intro: The wiggling knobs that bring a patch to life. These nodes generate or reshape a signal on the sapphire Modulator/CV cable, which can plug into almost any parameter in the app.
cards: A slow, repeating wave, sine, triangle, saw up, saw down, square, or sample-and-hold, that you plug into almost any knob in the patch to make it move on its own, in time with the music if you like.
sync an LFO to a quarter note and wire it to a filter's cutoff for an automatic wobble.

Generates a new target value on a timer, then eases toward it using a smoothing amount, 0 for hard stepped changes, higher for a fully eased curve. Low/High rescale the range, and each node spawns with its own seed.
feed two Random nodes with different rates into separate destinations for uncorrelated wandering motion.
A 16-step sequencer whose value steps through hand-set slots once per set beat length, looping back to the start, with a smoothing option to ease between adjacent steps instead of jumping.
draw a rising-then-falling step shape and route it into a filter cutoff for a rhythmic sweep locked to the beat.
Combines two other modulator signals using one of ten operations, add, subtract, multiply, divide, min, max, average, and more, then scales and offsets the result.
multiply an LFO by a Random node so the wobble's depth itself wanders over time.
Tests two modulator inputs against each other using >, >=, <, <=, ==, or != and outputs a hard 1 or 0, with a tolerance value for the equality checks.
compare a Random node against a fixed threshold to fire an on/off switch at unpredictable moments.
Linearly remaps an input modulator from one span to a different output span, with an option to clamp the result inside the output bounds.
remap an LFO's 0..1 swing down to a narrow 0.3..0.7 band for a subtler wobble.
Runs an exponential moving average over an input modulator, with an amount knob setting the filter strength, taking the edge off a stepped or noisy source.
smooth a Pattern node's stepped output to turn a staircase into a gentle glide.
Mirrors an input modulator around a low/high pivot, so rises become falls and vice versa, and it still behaves correctly on signals that run outside the usual 0..1 range.
invert an LFO feeding one destination while the un-inverted LFO feeds another, so two parameters move oppositely together.
Reshapes an input modulator through a user-drawn transfer curve, with a mix knob blending between the raw input and the fully-curved result.
draw a steep S-curve to make a smooth LFO snap more decisively between its extremes.

title: Modulators, Control & Performance
intro: Knobs, pads, and hardware bridges meant to be touched live, plus the utility nodes that hold a modulation chain together.
cards: Scales how much of an incoming modulator's swing reaches its destination with a single depth knob from -1 to 1, at 0 the signal has no effect, negative values invert it while still scaling.
automate depth itself with a slow LFO to fade a modulation effect in and out over time.
A single manually-set control meant to be performed rather than left alone, with a curve exponent to ease the response in or out and an invert switch.
map Macro Knob to several destinations at once as a single "intensity" performance control for a whole patch.
A plain 0-to-1 fader, the simplest possible performance control, meant to be grabbed and pushed rather than automated.
map it to Reverb Mix for a single fader that wets or dries the whole patch.

A center-detent knob that swings -1 to +1 rather than 0 to 1, so its resting position genuinely means "no effect", ideal for anything you want to push both directions from a neutral center, like a pan or a pitch bend.
center it at rest and map it to a filter's LFO depth so turning either way adds wobble, and dead-center is silence.
A 2D performance pad, grab it with a mouse or trackpad to fling two parameters around at once, live. It can also record a path you drag out and loop it back for hands-free, repeating motion.
map X to a filter cutoff and Y to Glitch amount, then perform both with one finger.
A latching on/off switch, plain and simple, click once to flip it on, click again to flip it off.
gate a whole effects chain's Mix on and off with one click during a performance.
A momentary bang pad: it fires to 1 the instant you press it and drops back to 0 the instant you release, with its own flash so you can see exactly when it fired.
wire it into a Particle System's emit rate for a hand-triggered burst on demand.
A draggable, typeable number box with its own min/max/step range, for a performance control where you want to see and dial in an exact value rather than eyeball a knob's position.
set its range to match an LFO's rate in Hz for precise, typed-in tempo control.
A discrete multi-choice selector, pick one of a set number of options and it outputs that choice's position, evenly spaced across 0 to 1.
wire four choices into a Switcher's manual slot for one-click scene selection.
An 8-step rhythmic gate sequencer locked to the transport, toggle any of the 8 steps on or off and it outputs a 1-or-0 pulse in time with the beat, by default at sixteenth notes.
draw a syncopated pattern and route it into Glitch's Amount for a rhythmic stutter locked to the beat.
MIDI Learn for a single physical control on your USB MIDI hardware, click Learn, twist the knob, and it remembers that device's exact channel and controller number.
map a hardware filter-cutoff knob to sweep a Blur radius live during a performance.
Turns a MIDI pad hit into a decaying envelope pulse (Pad mode, bound to one note), or reports whichever note was last played on the channel (Keyboard mode).
trigger a camera-shake or flash burst every time you hit a specific pad.
Moves a point along a shape over time, Circle, Line, Figure Eight, Helix, Spiral, or Lissajous, outputting separate X, Y, Z, and progress channels, tempo-synced by default.
send the X and Y outputs to a Geometry node's position to orbit an object in a circle.
Outputs one fixed, unmoving value, exists because math-utility nodes only take other modulators as input, so this supplies a literal number.
use it as a fixed offset added to an LFO to keep a modulation from ever reaching zero.
A zero-cost pass-through junction for a modulator cable, useful as a named point in a chain where you can read a live value meter or branch one signal to several destinations.
insert one mid-chain to visually confirm what value an LFO chain is actually producing.
Extracts a small color palette from a reference image or live video, clustering colors in Oklab space with sort, chroma, and mood-shaping controls (hue shift, saturation, brightness).
feed in a still-life photo and pipe its palette into every Ramp and material color in the patch for one cohesive mood.

title: Modulators, Audio/Note Bridges & Analysis
intro: The converters that translate between worlds, audio into control voltage, notes into control voltage, geometry into control voltage, and raw sound or image into a stream of numbers a patch can react to.
cards: Quantizes a continuous modulation signal into semitone steps, optionally snapped onto a chosen scale and root, with a glide option for portamento smoothing on the stepped output.
feed a slow Random node through it set to a major scale for generative, in-key melodic-feeling movement.
Converts an incoming note stream's pitch into a normalized control voltage, holding the last played note's pitch rather than falling back to zero on release, a pitch tracker, not a gate.
track incoming melody pitch and use it to modulate a filter cutoff so higher notes open the filter.
An envelope/amplitude follower that converts a live audio signal into a modulation signal, with gain, attack/release smoothing, and a peak/RMS detection mode.
feed a vocal or instrument track in and use the follower's output to pulse a Shape's scale in time with the performance.

Samples up to 16 points off a patched mesh and reports each one as its own X/Y/Z modulator, plus an overall centroid and spread, turning the literal shape of a piece of geometry into a bank of control voltages. Vertex, Scatter, and Contour sampling modes read different things off the source, and an offset control scrubs a read head across it without re- sampling.
sample 8 points off a spinning Torus and drive 8 separate effect params straight from its shape.
A simple free-running sine LFO with one control, rate in Hz, meant as a substitute for true per-note vibrato, since note events have no continuous pitch channel of their own.
patch it into an oscillator's fine-tune modulation input for a subtle, continuous pitch wobble.
Applies a classic ADSR contour to a continuous modulation signal rather than a note trigger, the "gate" is derived from the input crossing a threshold rather than a note-on/off.
feed a slow LFO in to get a rhythmic swell-and-release pulse instead of a raw sine wave.
Loads and plays back an audio file independently of the live mic/line input, exposing the same analysis taps as live input so a backing track can drive visuals deterministically.
load a pre-mixed track and drive the whole visual patch from it so a live performance is reproducible.
Listens to any audio and splits it into 8 frequency bands plus a transient onset trigger, the node that lets visuals genuinely react to music, band by band, hit by hit.
route a bass band into the Ocean node's amplitude so the sea pulses with the low end.
The visual mirror of Audio Analyze, reads brightness, color channels, saturation, hue, motion, and where the action is happening on screen, turning all of it into modulation.
drive a synth's pitch or filter straight from webcam motion for a fully vision-controlled instrument.

title: Output & Sharing
intro: The final door out, to your speakers, your screen, another app, or a real projector.
cards: The last node in every patch, sends your visuals and audio to the screen and speakers, and can record both to disk at once as an H.264 movie, ready to share or edit further.
hit Record on your finished Layer Stack and audio mix to bounce a performance straight to file.

Broadcasts whatever image, 3D render, or shader is plugged into it out to other Mac apps in real time, Resolume, OBS, TouchDesigner, MadMapper, via zero-copy GPU memory sharing, with a customizable server name.
send your generative render live into a VJ app like Resolume for a live show while still tweaking the patch in Infinite.

A projection-mapping and warping node for driving real projectors, 4-corner perspective warping or a subdivided mesh- grid warp, with built-in alignment test patterns for lining up a physical projector.
use the Grid test pattern to line up a projector on an odd-shaped surface, then switch to real content once corners are pinned.

Listens on a network port for OSC messages matching an address pattern and reports the last value received as a modulator, remapped to a low/high range, it patches in exactly like an LFO or Random node, just driven by another app or device instead.
drive Bloom's amount from a TouchOSC fader on your phone for a wireless second pair of hands.

The one node with no output at all: it reads whatever modulator is patched into it and sends its value out over the network as an OSC message, so a lighting console, Max/MSP patch, or another OSC-speaking app can react to what's happening inside Infinite.
send Audio Analyze's bass band out over OSC to pulse a real DMX light rig on every beat.

title: The Field Language, Programmable Nodes
intro: The newest, deepest chapter in the palette: five nodes that don't offer a preset list at all, they offer a text box. Write a little math, and Infinite compiles it straight to the right engine for the job.

Five nodes let you write your own behavior directly into a node instead of picking from a fixed list. Type a small block of code, a kernel, and Infinite runs it automatically, once for everything it needs to touch: once per point on a mesh, once per pixel on screen, once per sample of audio. You never say how many times or how fast to run it, the node figures that out from what your code actually touches. It is a tiny programming language built for exactly one job, and it turns each of these five nodes into a blank canvas instead of a fixed preset list.
cards: Runs your kernel once per pixel, compiled straight to a real GPU shader, an image generator or effect you write from scratch instead of picking off a shelf. It can declare its own state, a persistent texture it remembers between frames, so feedback-style effects that need memory are possible in one self-contained node.
write a kernel that reads its own state and blends in the new frame for a self-contained feedback trail in one node.

Runs your kernel once per vertex of an incoming mesh, letting you rewrite position, normal, color, or any custom attribute with plain math instead of picking from a fixed deformer list. Leave the geometry input empty and it generates its own points instead, acting as a source.
write P.y += bass to turn any mesh into a shape that visibly pulses with the low end.

A pure generator: builds 3D point geometry entirely from your kernel, starting from a topology scaffold, points, a plane, a sphere, a torus, that your code then reshapes. Presets like Fibonacci Sphere, Spiral, and Torus Knot show what's possible from just a formula.
start from the Fibonacci Sphere preset and instance small spheres on the result for an evenly-scattered point cloud.

A polyphonic synthesizer whose entire voice algorithm is a kernel you write yourself, run per-voice on the audio thread, your own oscillator, FM algorithm, or wavetable scheme as plain math instead of a fixed engine.
write a two-operator FM kernel from scratch and hear it respond to MIDI Notes like any other synth.

Runs a kernel once per audio sample as a custom effect, declare a bit of state for a delay line or filter memory, declare a param for an automatic modulatable knob, and write the DSP math yourself instead of hunting for the right built-in. Also cataloged in Chapter Twelve alongside the rest of the effects shelf.
write a simple one-pole low-pass in a few lines and compare it against the built-in Audio Filter.
